places.name: Upton (East Knoyle) & Donhead St Mary, Shaftesbury Border, Wilts
places.grid: 5 mi N of Shaftesbury • TNA CP 40/636, 656 & 664
places.desc: Shaftesbury Abbey border corridor where commercial grazier John Lussh of Upton sued Gylbert Brytt of Donhead St Mary (adjoining Melbury Abbas) in 1420, traded with Salisbury butchers in 1425, and died 1425–26 (executors proved 1427).

places.name: Stour Provost (Stoure Prewes), Blackmore Vale, Dorset
places.grid: 4.5 mi NW of Melbury Abbas • TNA CP 40/724 rot. 388f
places.desc: Blackmore Vale parish where plaintiff John Lusshe sued husbandman Thomas Fraunceys in Hilary Term 1442 (20 Henry VI) for a locked chest containing £40—matching Edmond Lushe's £40 capital assessment 81 years later.

places.name: Hinton St Mary (Henton Abbatis), Blackmore Vale, Dorset
places.grid: Adjoining Sturminster Newton • TNA CP 40/758 rot. 1195d
places.desc: Stour valley parish where surviving executor John Lusshe sued husbandman John Gervays in Trinity Term 1450 (28 Henry VI) for 8 marks, 6s. 4d. (£5 13s. 0d.), right beside Sturminster Newton.

places.name: Tisbury (Tessebury / Tyssebury), Shaftesbury Abbey Manor, Wilts
places.grid: 6.5 mi NE of Shaftesbury • WRS 45:44, CP 40/724 & 776
places.desc: Cross-border Shaftesbury Abbey manor where John le Lusshe was taxed 12d. in Sept. 1332, husbandman John Lusshe stood bonded with Tisbury miller John Stephenys for 40s. (1442), and William Lusshe was sued for 10 marks by Henry Leye (1455).

places.name: Oakley Farm (Ocle / Okeley) in Tisbury, Shaftesbury Abbey Estate, Wilts
places.desc: Ancient Shaftesbury Abbey border farmstead: in Sept. 1332 John le Lusshe was taxed 12d. two lines below Alexander de Ocle (Oakley), and 148 years later husbandman John Lusshe of Oakley in Tisbury was sued alongside Sedgehill and Dorset farmers in Hilary Term 1480.

places.name: St. Paul's Trinity & Hants Harbour, Trinity Bay, NL
places.grid: St. Paul's Anglican PRs • Benjamin Lester & Co.
places.desc: Pre-established Protestant Dwyer fishing cluster in Trinity Bay (including John Dwyer, servant to Poole merchants Benjamin Lester & Co., 1806 marriages of John & James Dwyer, and John Dwyer d. 1855 age 26)—testing Model B for Capt. John Alexander Dwyer's origin in the same bay as bride Caroline Bemister Thorne.

places.name: Bookham Farm & Knoll, Buckland Newton, Dorset

places.name: Alton Pancras, Cerne Valley, Dorset
places.grid: 1.5 miles south of Bookham • Salisbury Peculiar
places.desc: Tudor home of kinsmen Robert & John Squyer (1524–76 wills) and post-Spring 1678 parish of Gen 11 John Squire Senr. (bur. 1703), Roger Squire (bur. 1710/11), and Gen 10 John Junr. & Eleanor [Elnar].

places.name: Piddletrenthide, Piddle Valley, Dorset
places.grid: 1.5 miles east across the ridge • 1732/33 Register
places.desc: Village where 23-year-old Gen 9 Philip Squire buried infant daughter Margaret (Feb. 23, 1732/33) and wife Mary (Mar. 14, 1732/33), surviving with infant son John Squire.

places.name: Shipton Gorge, West Dorset
places.desc: 1525 tax roll village of Robert Akerman (G 10) and 1539–42 muster village of Jn, Ste, and Hen Akerman.

places.name: Bothenhampton, Loders & Bridport, Dorset
places.grid: DHC PE/BT & SP 12/56 • Rope & Net District
places.desc: 1539–69 muster and tax home of archers Hen Akerman (G 4) & Ric Akerman, Loders taxpayer John Akerman (1594 G 3), and 18th-century rope- and fishing-net hub supplying ships to Newfoundland.

places.name: St. John the Baptist Church, Broadwindsor, Dorset
places.grid: 6 miles NW of Bridport • 1745 Baptism Register
places.desc: Baptism parish of Bonavista lay minister Abraham Akerman Sr. (baptized 1745 to Daniel & Jean [Jane] Akerman, matching his 1822 burial at age 77).

places.name: St. Giles Church, Chideock — Cottage "Lushes"
places.desc: Coastal Dorset village where Gen 8 John Squire (aged 72 in 1802 holding a 99-year lease on a churchside cottage coincidentally named "Lushes") & Elizabeth baptized pioneer Simon Squire on April 2, 1769.

places.name: East Melbury & St. Thomas's Church, Melbury Abbas
places.desc: Ancestral root of Gen 16 Edmond Lusshe (£40 in Oct. 1523 [top 1.7% of Dorset]; G 20 in 1525; steel Almain rivets armour in 1539–42), Gen 15 John Lusshe (1572 £20 will), Gen 12 John Lush (1673 £50 will) & Gen 9 Thomas Lush.

places.name: Compton Abbas, Blackmore Vale, Dorset
places.desc: Bundled with Melbury Abbas in the Sept. 1544 Arundell Manor Grant; home of Gen 12 Nicholas & Mary Lush, Gen 11 Edmund Lush (bapt. Aug. 1676; married Mary Lawrence Apr. 14, 1707), and shared family burials.

places.name: Fontmell Magna, Blackmore Vale, Dorset

places.name: Shaftesbury Abbey & Holy Trinity Church, Dorset

places.name: Okeford Fitzpaine & Sturminster Newton, Dorset
places.desc: Blackmore Vale towns linked by the 1719/20 legal property bond between Edmund Lush of Okeford Fitzpaine and his eldest son Robert Lush 'of Sturminster Newton'.

places.name: Ashmore, Cranborne Chase, Dorset
places.desc: Hilltop Dorset village where Gen 10 Robert & Elizabeth Lush baptized Gen 9 Thomas Lush on December 30, 1725.

places.name: St. Mary's Church, Motcombe, Dorset
places.desc: English departure parish where Newfoundland pioneer John Lush was baptized April 30, 1775 (right below neighbour Ann Blandford), and where 78-year-old cousin George Lush lived in 1871.

places.name: Wimborne Minster, East Dorset
places.desc: Baptism parish of Greenspond pioneer David Goulding (Jan. 17, 1773), maternal grandfather of Mary Goulding Lush.

places.name: All Saints Merriott & Crewkerne, Somerset
places.desc: Somerset home of 1569 armour-holder Thomas Lawrens Sr., archer Peter Langdon, Thomas Lawrence Jr. (d. 1637), John Lawrence & Joane Langdon (1656), William Lawrence & Sarah Shore (1657) & Mary Lawrence (1690).

places.name: Bower Chalke, South Wiltshire
places.desc: Village of yeoman John Newman, whose 1794/95 will left £120 to 'my sisters son John Lush, now living in the parish of Motcomb'.

places.name: Port of Waterford, Ireland
places.desc: Main Irish departure port connecting Fethard and South Tipperary to West Country merchant ships sailing to Twillingate, Newfoundland.

places.name: Ilé Ọ̀ṣùnkọ́tì (At Osunkoti), Idamudu I, Emure-Ekiti
places.desc: Hereditary Osukoti quarter-chieftaincy seat founded at Emure Ijaloke (c. 1780) and held by Chief Daniel Ogunlusi Kolade (K4) and Chief John Aderibigbe Kolade (1968).

places.name: Ojomu Akeregun, Odo-Emure IV, Emure-Ekiti
places.desc: Senior kingmaker (Ìwàrẹ̀fà) seat ('Near Ojumu's House') of High Chief Ojomu Arintokun, High Chief Ojomu Ogedu, and the Late Chief Ojomu (father of Madam Lydia Olugbe Kolade).

places.name: Oko Ọ̀sẹ Kọ́ládé — River Ose Farm Estate (#35)
places.desc: Hereditary family farm estate ('Kolade's Farmstead on the River Ose') anchoring Generation 5 patriarch Kọ́ládé / [Ògún]kọ́ládé.

places.name: Ijebu-Owo Palace (Ojomo Oluda), Owo Kingdom
places.grid: 22 km east of Emure • c. 1880 Carved Effigy
places.desc: Royal palace of High Chief Ojomo Agunloye I (d. c. 1880, dated by his life-sized carved wooden àkó burial effigy), father of Olajenboye, and St. Patrick's school town of Pa Joseph Kolade.

places.name: Benin City & Ago Olumoye, Edo State (CMS Bookshops)
places.desc: Early career hub where Chief John A. Kolade (1922) and Pa Joseph O. Kolade (1933) joined C.M.S. Bookshops, and where Joseph married Madam Lydia Olugbe in 1942 (birth of Victor Olusoji Kolade).

places.name: Ondo, Ado-Ekiti & Ibadan Corridor, Nigeria
places.grid: St. Stephen's Ondo, Adeoyo Hospital & Ado-Ekiti
places.desc: Regional corridor where Pa Joseph Kolade reorganized C.M.S. Bookshops (1946–58), Mama Dudu ran her Ondo ẹ̀kọ and Ado–Emure wholesale bakery network, Canon Awosika baptized Eric Bamidele (Oct. 1947), and Chief John A. Kolade trained at Adeoyo Hospital.

places.name: Bonavista, Bonavista Bay, Newfoundland
places.desc: Home for 30+ years of Anglican lay minister Abraham Akerman Sr. (1745–1822), who signed 'A Ackerman' when officiating the Aug. 18, 1798 wedding of his daughter Jane Akerman to Simon Squires Sr. (1769–1832).

places.name: Greenspond, Bonavista Bay, Newfoundland
places.desc: Granite island outport settled by Motcombe pioneer John Lush (1775–1827) & Elizabeth Jane Wood, David Goulding (1773–1826), May 26, 1840 wedding of Thomas Lush & Mary Goulding, and 1857 St. Stephen's timber haul.

places.name: Hillview, Trinity Bay, Newfoundland
places.grid: Southwest Arm, Trinity Bay • Thorne Family Root
places.desc: Birthplace of matriarch Caroline Bemister Thorne (c. 1837–1906, daughter of Somerset pioneer Richard Thorne & Betsy George), who married Irish pioneer Capt. John Alexander Dwyer c. 1856.

places.name: Herring Neck & Twillingate, Notre Dame Bay, NL
places.desc: Northern harbour of Simon & Julia Squires (1836 census) and c. 1856–1907 home of Irish Methodist pioneer Capt. John Alexander Dwyer & Caroline Bemister Thorne.

places.name: Tilt Cove Copper Mine & Nipper's Harbour, NL
places.desc: Sept. 2, 1862 wedding harbour of Silas Squires & Sarah Jane Noble (Nipper's Harbour) and cliffside copper-mining town of William Lush, Polly Dwyer, Rev. Philip H. Lush (b. 1888) & miner Albert Dwyer (d. 1895).

places.name: Lushes Bight & Burlington / North West Arm, NL
places.grid: Notre Dame Bay & Green Bay Coves
places.desc: Sheltered inlet that still bears the family name (Lushes Bight on Long Island) and permanent Burlington / North West Arm home of William Lush (1845–1922) & Polly Dwyer (1863–1905).

places.name: Smiths Harbour, Green Bay, Newfoundland
places.desc: Home of Silas & William Squires, sawmill and medical-boat pioneer Albert Lush (1898–1980) & Florence White, Sept. 6, 1944 wedding of Pleman Squires & Ivy Lush, and birthplace of Merle Elizabeth Squires.

places.name: Portland & Kennebunkport, Maine, USA
places.grid: New England Ministry • Rev. Philip H. Lush
places.desc: New England ministry home of Tilt Cove-born Rev. Philip Henry Lush (1888–1967, son of William Lush & Polly Dwyer) and his sons Earle, Aubrey, and Herbert Lush.

places.name: Sudbury, Northern Ontario, Canada
places.desc: Site of the family's earliest mainland Canadian foothold, where Smiths Harbour cousin William Silas Squires married Ethel Jane Brown in 1913.

places.name: Pine Hills Cemetery (Section A, Lot 2436H), Scarborough
places.desc: Family memorial site: 2026 charcoal granite monument honoring Victor Olusoji Kolade (1942–2017) of Emure-Ekiti, Nigeria & Merle Elizabeth Kolade, née Squires (1944–2025) of Smith's Harbour, NL.

places.name: Toronto, Ontario, Canada
places.desc: Home of Victor Olusoji Kolade & Merle Elizabeth Squires (married 1973) and living Generation 1 household of Victor Olutayo Kolade & Abigail Salole.

events.title: Oldest Ancestral Estate Record (694 Years Ago): "John le Lusshe — 12d" Taxed at Tisbury / Oakley Before the Black Death
events.diplomatic: [TNA E 179/196/8, Sept. 1332 Wiltshire Lay Subsidy (15th), Dunworth Hundred — Tisbury (Tysseburye), WRS Vol. 45, p. 44, col. 2] Alexander de Ocle — 20d | Walter Warner — 3s | John le Lusshe — 12d | Thomas de Toteredehulle — 4s | Edward le Wyke — 8s 10d | John Boterstake — 4s | David de Seghulle — 8s.
events.synthesis: Pushes the documented Lusshe estate and surname horizon back 694 years into the early reign of King Edward III—sixteen years before the Black Death of 1348! Enrolled under Shaftesbury Abbey's manor of Tisbury just two lines below Alexander de Ocle (Oakley in Tisbury) and four lines above David de Seghulle (Sedgehill), taxpayer John le Lusshe (assessed 12d. on 15s. of surplus livestock/grain) captures both the Anglo-Norman 'le Lusshe' origin of the Lush surname and the exact Oakley-in-Tisbury farmstead strip still held by John Lusshe 148 years later in 1480.
events.immunity: Verified verbatim on p. 44 of Crowley's Wiltshire Tax List of 1332 (the sole Lusshe household in all of 1332 Wiltshire); graded conservatively as Pre-Tudor Monastic Estate & Surname Continuity.
